MT-2027-LC426.title: Establish the Office of Public Information Requests
MT-2027-LC426.policyArea: Public Officers and Employees, State Government
MT-2027-LC426.aiSummary: Would create an Office of Public Information Requests to handle public records requests in state government.

MT-2027-LC933.title: Generally revise public records request deadline laws
MT-2027-LC933.aiSummary: It would change the rules for how fast public records requests must be handled in Montana.

MT-2027-LC927.title: Revise laws related to financial discrimination
MT-2027-LC927.aiSummary: Would revise Montana laws about financial discrimination, which means unfair treatment based on money matters. The only listed action is that a drafter was assigned on 2026-11-03.

MT-2027-LC912.title: Generally revise laws related to minors' online safety
MT-2027-LC912.aiSummary: Would revise Montana laws on online safety for minors, or people under 18. It would affect rules for how children and teens use the internet and online services.

MT-2027-LC906.title: Provide for the data center transparency act
MT-2027-LC906.aiSummary: Would create rules for data centers and require more transparency, which means clearer public information about them.

MT-2027-LC636.title: Revise distribution lists for occupational licensing
MT-2027-LC636.aiSummary: The bill would change who gets sent notices and other information about occupational licenses.

MT-2027-LC549.title: Revise special education finance laws to increase the total SPED allocation and SPED allowable cost payments to districts and coops
MT-2027-LC549.policyArea: Appropriations, Education - School Finance, Education - Special Education
MT-2027-LC549.aiSummary: Would change Montana special education funding rules to increase the total special education allocation and the allowed cost payments to school districts and cooperatives.

MT-2027-LC540.title: Revise school funding laws to improve consistency and clarity of terminology
MT-2027-LC540.aiSummary: The bill would revise school funding laws in Montana to make the terms used in them more consistent and clear.

MT-2027-LC513.title: Clarify requirements for trapping/hunting mentors and apprentice license eligibility
MT-2027-LC513.aiSummary: The bill would clarify the rules for hunting and trapping mentors and who can get an apprentice license in Montana.

MT-2027-LC480.title: Extend voluntary out-of-home protective placement of child
MT-2027-LC480.aiSummary: Would let a child stay in a voluntary out-of-home protective placement for a longer time.

MT-2027-LC447.title: Provide a statutory appropriation for the statewide public safety communications system
MT-2027-LC447.aiSummary: The bill would set up a statutory appropriation, which lets the Department of Justice spend money for the statewide public safety communications system without a separate yearly budget step. It would also move money into the state account for that system, including $5.33 million for the fiscal year starting July 1, 2027, and $5.23 million each year from July 1, 2028, through June 30, 2035. The act would take effect July 1, 2027.

MT-2027-LC432.title: Eliminate the authority to construct buildings report
MT-2027-LC432.aiSummary: Would remove the authority to issue a report on building construction, under state government rules.

MT-2027-LC393.title: Make voter address verification notices forwardable
MT-2027-LC393.aiSummary: The bill would change Montana rules for voter registration list checks and address notices. It would require election administrators to use forwardable, first-class confirmation notices when checking voter addresses and handling notices that come back undelivered or get no response. If a voter still does not respond after 30 days, the voter would be moved to the inactive list until the address is verified or the voter updates their registration.

MT-2027-LC366.title: Revise ballot language for levy or bond impact on residence
MT-2027-LC366.policyArea: Education - School Finance, Elections, Local Finance
MT-2027-LC366.aiSummary: The bill would change ballot and notice language for school and local tax elections so people can see the expected property tax impact on a home. It would require estimates for homes worth $100,000, $300,000, $600,000, and the county median home value for a main residence, and it would let a district or local government use a different home value in some cases. It would also require the state revenue department to provide an online tool for calculating the impact and for school districts and other taxing bodies to post that tool on their websites.

MT-2027-LC324.title: Revise firearm accessories and firearm laws
MT-2027-LC324.aiSummary: The bill would change Montana laws on short-barreled rifles, shotguns, firearms, and silencers. It would remove the ban on hunting with a silencer or muffling device, update state references to silencer registration under federal law, and remove the penalty for having a sawed-off firearm. It would also say the wildlife department may not regulate firearms, firearm accessories, or ammunition, while still allowing some hunting rules and safety limits.

MT-2027-LC222.title: Prohibit, with exceptions, law enforcement from wearing masks
MT-2027-LC222.aiSummary: The bill would limit law enforcement officers from wearing masks, with some exceptions. It affects police and other law enforcement agencies.
